problems.note: The three choices are distinguished only by their pictures. Read aloud, each choice says just its label ("1/3 of the circle", etc.), so a child who can't see the picture can answer from the label alone. Consider having the narration or choice text describe the shading (for example, "1 of 3 equal parts shaded") so the answer depends on the fraction, not on wording.

Same issue as tap-2: the correct rectangle is identifiable by its label alone ("3/8 of the rectangle"), so the picture is not needed to answer. Spoken choice text should describe the parts shaded and the total parts so the item can be solved by ear.

The item asks for pieces left after eating (8 minus 3), which is subtraction practice rather than reading a fraction. It is a loose fit for the skill "represent fractions". Consider rewording to ask a fraction question, such as what fraction of the pan is left (5/8), or keep it as a clearly labelled warm-up.

The picture shows 3 whole chocolate bars (3 × 🍫) but not the cutting into 4 equal pieces per person, so the answer 3/4 is not visible in the picture. The narration explains it, but the item is harder than its difficulty 3 label suggests for a child who listens only. Consider a picture of each bar cut into 4 equal parts with one person's share marked.
